title: iNaturalist Observation Confidence by Species
dataSources: Catch trips (`outdoor:trip`), hunt map activity (`hunt:map`), foraging observations (`forage:observation`), smoker sessions (`cook:smoker`), harvest queues (`outdoor:queue`).
app: Fishing, hunting, foraging, and outdoor-cooking telemetry — Fishbrain catch logs, onX Hunt map exports, iNaturalist observations, and ThermoWorks smoker probes — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs, exports, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=forage:observation species=* community_id_agrees=*
| stats count as total, sum(eval(if(community_id_agrees="yes",1,0))) as matched by species
| eval community_agreement_pct=round(100*matched/total,1)
| sort - community_agreement_pct
description: Measures the percentage of foraging observations that end with community agreement by species.
value: Completion and exception percentages make it easier to spot which species are helping or hurting foraging observations.
implementation: Store a normalized flag for `community agreement` on `forage:observation` events and summarize the hit rate by `species`.
visualization: Table of species with percentage of foraging observations ending with community agreement.
grandmaExplanation: It reveals how often community agreement happens for each species so you can see where foraging observations go smoothly or get stuck.
